Om. “If it is said that this is not the case due to the difference in the teachings, that is not so, because there is no contradiction in either.” Om. 1/1/27.

The earlier teaching is “the three-footed amṛta in the sky.” The later teaching, ending in the fifth case, is “the supreme sky.” Therefore, if it is said that one and the same object is not being described here, that is not so, because there is no contradiction in either, given their respective reference to the three and seven worlds. 27.
